about: The facts behind docs/superpowers/command-record.html. Edit this file, then run node frontend/scripts/ci/command-record.mjs (DECISIONS 2026-10-31 items 280 and 281). Each detail row's src says where its fact was read; it is not shown on the page. Glance: about 250 visible words. Detail rows: one plain line each, about 15 words at most.

stands.alt: The game's world is live for players, and every check is green.
stands.caption: Live for everyone, and every check is green: 31 October 2026.

better.sub: Since you handed over on 27 October.

cards.alt: A player steps out of an invisible box, free.
cards.caption: Placing a block can no longer trap you in an invisible box.

cards.alt: The title screen offers Continue, with New World below.
cards.caption: Continue on the title takes you straight back to your world.

cards.alt: The Shadow Dragon flies over a glowing ring on the ground where its attack will land; the player steps out of it.
cards.caption: The Shadow Dragon marks the ground before each attack lands.

cards.alt: An iPhone and an iPad show the YOU DIED screen, not a crash.
cards.caption: Dying on iPhone or iPad should no longer crash. Check it on yours.

cards.alt: A player stuck in rock is lifted to open ground, and a player at the bottom of a deep hole stays there.
cards.caption: Stuck in rock? You are moved clear.

cards.alt: On a big Mac screen the game draws about 4.2 million pixels where it drew 7.7 million: two bars to scale.
cards.caption: Big Macs draw half the pixels, so they should run cooler.

cards.alt: A grass block with clear top and side faces, and a game screen that is almost all world with small on-screen panels.
cards.caption: Blocks have a new look, and the screen is far less cluttered.

cards.alt: A block mined from stone travels to the wall you build.
cards.caption: Building uses the blocks you mine.

bugs.alt: Over 40 real bugs found, 8 of them big. All 8 are fixed in code and all 12 fix lanes have landed; two wait on your iPhone and iPad.
bugs.caption: All 8 big ones are fixed and all 12 fix lanes landed. Two need your iPhone and iPad.

now.alt: Done: rewards match what really happened; saves that fail now tell you; the game remembers your squad and shrines. Now: chasing a freeze when Start is clicked before the world is built. Also landed: sound on iPhone and iPad, and better tests. Next: the First Night.
now.caption: Just shipped: rewards, saves, iPhone and iPad sound, better tests. Now: a Start-click freeze. Next: the First Night.

you.alt: Three things for you: play on iPhone and iPad, mix the sound by ear, and if you like, three deep reviews on account 2.
you.caption: Only you can do these. Nothing is blocked on them.

hunt.title: The bug hunt
hunt.sub: After your invisible box, a deep audit hunted such bugs: 47 rechecked, 40 confirmed.

rows.text: A right-click sealed you inside your own block.
Every death on iPhone or iPad crashed the game.
A returning player never got their world back; Start began a fresh one.
Loading a world could drop you into a cave or out of the world.
Recovering from a graphics crash wiped your quests and revived a slain dragon.
After a load, an unhittable dragon chased a level-1 hero.
Your bound squad is never saved.
On touch, the Settings gear never opened.
Two browser tabs on one world overwrote each other's progress.
rows.src: registry AUDIT:persistence:two-tabs-clobber-world, raised MED to HIGH, closedBy 66d83473 (PR #65)

groups.title: Big ones the fix lanes found

rows.text: On touch, Respawn and Keep exploring ignored a finger.
A respawn could drop you blind from high up, sometimes into rock.
A body clipped into rock above a cave stayed stuck there.

lanes.title: The twelve fix lanes, all landed

rows.text: Quick wins: iPhone death crash, Show Stats on touch, effects setting restored, Settings gear.
Every world switch reloads into that world; Continue on the title.
Each world keeps its own squad and shrines, and they are saved.
Falling out of the world is judged at its floor, with one shared recovery.
One rule decides when keys and taps act on the game.
Build tools that do what they say.
Rewards, sounds and tallies follow what actually happened, not the click.
